meta.purpose: Honest literature and prior-art assessment of three candidate 2027 project concepts for GEMS-Taiwan (high school, iGEM), against both the peer-reviewed literature and the iGEM 2026 cohort. Written so the public report does not claim novelty it has not checked.
meta.assessedBy: literature and prior-art pass; PubMed, Consensus, web search, plus the 106 team files in research/teams/
teamConstraints: Risk Group 1 organisms only: E. coli, B. subtilis, S. cerevisiae, Komagataella pastoris
No human samples of any kind
No isolating or sequencing from environmental samples
Existing capability: CcaSR green-light two-component system in B. subtilis WB800; self-built light-plate hardware
Track record: Best Measurement and Best Hardware, 2026 High School section

howToReadVerdicts.genuinely novel: No published work does this thing at all, in any application.
howToReadVerdicts.novel in this application: The method or mechanism is published elsewhere; applying it to this target or matrix is not. Supports a paper only if the application itself is the contribution and is done rigorously.
howToReadVerdicts.incremental: Both method and application are published; the contribution would be added rigour, scale, or standardisation. Can support a methods or measurement note, rarely a full paper.
howToReadVerdicts.already done: The closest prior work does substantially the thing proposed. Does not support a novelty claim.

threeKindsOfNoveltyClaim.note: The brief asked these be kept distinct, because only some support a paper.
threeKindsOfNoveltyClaim.nobodyHasPublishedThis: Strongest. Supports a full paper. Of the three concepts, only one narrow mechanistic slice of Concept A qualifies.
threeKindsOfNoveltyClaim.nobodyHasPublishedThisInThisApplication: Medium. Supports a paper only when the application is itself hard or consequential, and the measurement is rigorous. Concept B's semiconductor-effluent target and part of Concept A sit here.
threeKindsOfNoveltyClaim.nobodyHasPublishedThisAtThisScaleOrRigou: Weakest. Supports a methods note, measurement note, or registered part descriptor. Concept C sits here, and so does the realistically achievable version of Concept A.

igemCohortCheck.method: Grepped all 106 files in research/teams/ for optogenetics, metals, semiconductor, wafer, biofilm, stress-reporter and toxicity-panel terms, then read the relevant team files.
findings: Concept A is directly contested inside the 2026 cohort: McGill (6040) and SMS-Shenzhen (6165). See concepts.A.priorArt.

Concept B: no 2026 team runs a multi-promoter stress-reporter panel for mixture or integrated toxicity. The nearest is HongKong-JSS (6158), MerMAID, a single MerR-based mercury assay, high school, which shows the division does single-analyte metal biosensing but not panels. Concept B is uncontested within the cohort; it is the literature that kills it.

Concept C: no 2026 team uses silicon wafers, or any defined reference surface, as an assay substrate. UOregon (6041) mentions silicon only as a wastewater contaminant alongside PFAS and nitrate. Concept C is uncontested within the cohort.
Note for the team's own records: GEMS-Taiwan is 6072 in this dataset, project ReLEAF.

A.title: Light-gated metal capture and release
A.asProposed: Use an optogenetic switch (CcaSR or similar) to control binding and release of gallium, indium or germanium by an engineered microbial surface-display or secreted binding protein, so a recovery column is regenerated with light instead of acid elution.

priorArt.axis: light-controlled affinity capture and release (protein target, not metal)
priorArt.citation: Mayrhofer P, Anneser MR, Schira K, Sommer CA, Theobald I, Schlapschy M, Achatz S, Skerra A (2024). Protein purification with light via a genetically encoded azobenzene side chain. Nature Communications 15:10693.
priorArt.whatItDid: The Azo-tag: a short peptide containing the unnatural amino acid p-(phenylazo)-L-phenylalanine. trans-Pap binds an alpha-cyclodextrin column; 355 nm light switches it to cis, and the protein elutes under plain physiological buffer with no competing agent and no harsh buffer. Named Excitography.
priorArt.whyItMatters: This is the single most important paper for Concept A. The exact headline claim 'light replaces chemical elution in affinity chromatography' is already published, in Nature Communications, for protein targets. Concept A cannot claim that framing as new. It can only claim the metal-ion version.

priorArt.axis: light-controlled affinity capture and release (protein target)
priorArt.citation: Prodromou R, et al. (2023). Molecular Engineering of Cyclic Azobenzene-Peptide Hybrid Ligands for the Purification of Human Blood Factor VIII via Photo-Affinity Chromatography. Advanced Functional Materials.
priorArt.whatItDid: Cyclic azobenzene-peptide ligands on translucent chromatographic beads; >6 mg Factor VIII per mL resin, photo-isomerisation in under 30 s at 420-450 nm, >90% yield and >95% purity using a single mobile phase.
priorArt.whyItMatters: Second independent demonstration that photo-affinity chromatography works as a real separation process. 'Regenerate a column with light' is an established idea, not a new one.
priorArt.unverified: DOI not captured; volume and page numbers not confirmed. Verify before citing.

priorArt.axis: light-triggered release from a column
priorArt.citation: Agrawal K, et al. (2026). Light-Activated Molecular Purification (LAMP): A Photo-Responsive Affinity-Chromatography Protocol for Recombinant Protein Purification. Current Protocols.
priorArt.whatItDid: 6xHis-PhoCl1-POI fusion on Ni-NTA; light cleaves PhoCl1, the His-tagged barrel stays on the resin and the protein of interest is released. >90% purity.
priorArt.whyItMatters: A third, mechanistically different route to light-triggered elution, published as a standard protocol. Reinforces that the concept's framing is mature.

priorArt.axis: LIGHT-GATED BINDING AND RELEASE OF A METAL ION - closest hit on the decisive axis
priorArt.citation: Mutluturk E, et al. (2025). Spiropyran-Functionalized Polydimethylsiloxane Sponges for Reversible Adsorption of Metal Ions. ACS Applied Polymer Materials.
priorArt.whatItDid: Spiropyran photoswitch (0.23% loading) in a PDMS sponge. Spiropyran isomerises reversibly to merocyanine; merocyanine complexes Al3+, Zn2+, Fe3+, Co2+, Sn2+, Hg2+, Ca2+, Mg2+. Fe3+ capacity 2.60 +/- 0.15 mg/g. Ions are retrieved by rinsing under visible light; 5 cycles without fatigue.
priorArt.whyItMatters: THIS IS THE PAPER THAT CONSTRAINS CONCEPT A MOST TIGHTLY. Light-modulated reversible metal-ion capture and light-assisted release is already published. The remaining gap is narrower than it looks: it is specifically the PROTEIN or WHOLE-CELL version, and specifically Ga/In/Ge. Concept A must not claim 'light-gated metal capture and release' as new in general terms. The capacity is also instructive: 2.60 mg/g is low, which is what photoswitch-based capture tends to give because the switch occupies most of the material.

priorArt.axis: light-gated metal ion binding and release (small molecule)
priorArt.citation: Reversible ON/OFF and OFF/ON, light-stimulated binding, or release processes of metal cations from isatin diarylhydrazone complexes in solution. Journal of Photochemistry and Photobiology A (2022).
priorArt.whatItDid: Photochemical isomerisation of isatin diarylhydrazone ligands switches metal-cation binding on and off in solution, in both directions.
priorArt.whyItMatters: Independent confirmation that light-switchable metal coordination is established coordination chemistry. Only the biological implementation is open.

priorArt.axis: light-gated selective ion extraction
priorArt.citation: Ghosh A, et al. (2026). Light-Controlled Functions with Metal-Organic Capsules: From Guest Release to Catalysis, Separation, and Molecular Transport. Accounts of Chemical Research.
priorArt.whatItDid: Account of azobenzene-based photoswitchable metal-organic capsules, including selective lithium-ion extraction using a photoswitchable sandwich architecture, and light-gated selective molecular separations.
priorArt.whyItMatters: Selective, light-driven extraction of a technologically critical metal (Li) is published. Concept A cannot claim 'light-driven selective recovery of a critical metal' as a category.

priorArt.axis: light-controlled CELL HARVESTING with the team's own CcaSR system - and the precedent McGill did not have
priorArt.citation: Nakajima M, Abe K, Ferri S, Sode K (2016). Development of a light-regulated cell-recovery system for non-photosynthetic bacteria. Microbial Cell Factories 15:31.
priorArt.whatItDid: CcaS/CcaR green-light two-component system from Synechocystis sp. PCC6803, with the chromophore cassette co-expressed, driving Antigen 43 from PcpcG2 in E. coli. Green light causes self-aggregation and precipitation; approximately 80% of the culture recovered by simple decantation.
priorArt.whyItMatters: Two consequences. First, light-controlled harvesting of engineered cells by induced aggregation was published in 2016, ten years before McGill's 2026 project, and with THE SAME CcaSR system GEMS-Taiwan already runs. Second, it means Concept A absolutely cannot fall back on 'light-controlled harvesting' as its novelty: that route is occupied twice over, once in the literature and once in this competition.

priorArt.axis: iGEM 2026 - optogenetics + surface display + critical-metal recovery
priorArt.citation: McGill, iGEM 2026 team 6040, project LanTurn (Undergrad, Canada). Nominated Best Entrepreneurship and Best Biomanufacturing.
priorArt.whatItDid: S. cerevisiae EBY100 displaying lanmodulin variants via Aga1-Aga2 for selective rare-earth binding, PLUS a blue-light VP16-EL222 / C120 circuit driving truncated FLO1 so REE-loaded cells flocculate on command and settle by gravity instead of centrifugation. Light-induced flocculation 66-75% vs 24-25% dark controls; display confirmed by flow cytometry and confocal microscopy. Full techno-economic analysis, 11.83-20.58 USD/kg REO, Ashram tailings NPV case, seven sensitivity analyses.
priorArt.whyItMatters: The COMBINATION of optogenetics, microbial surface display and critical-metal recovery is already occupied in this competition, by a team that did it well and got nominated for it. Judges who followed 2026 will know this project. Concept A must cite McGill explicitly and state its distinction precisely, or it will read as a high-school restatement of LanTurn.
priorArt.theDistinctionThatRemains: McGill used light to control HARVESTING OF THE CELLS. Concept A proposes light to control BINDING AND RELEASE OF THE METAL ION ITSELF. That is a real mechanistic difference. It is also the whole of the difference.

priorArt.axis: iGEM 2026 - high school, selective biosorption of critical metals from real industrial wastewater
priorArt.citation: SMS-Shenzhen, iGEM 2026 team 6165, project kisMET (High School, China). Nominated Best New Composite Part.
priorArt.whatItDid: Komagataeibacter rhaeticus decorating its own bacterial cellulose with a secreted fusion of signal peptide + carbohydrate-binding module + HiBiT tag + swappable ion-binding peptide, Golden Gate on pSEVA331 under a rhamnose-inducible promoter. Four SP/CBM scaffolds, eight-member ion-binding-peptide panel so specificity is swappable. Targets Li, Co, Ni, Mn in battery-recycling tail wastewater. Honest about what is design objective vs result.
priorArt.whyItMatters: Two lessons. First, a high-school team can do credible metal-binding work, so the division precedent exists and the bar is set. Second, and more useful: this report's own note on kisMET records that the conspicuous hole was the TOTAL ABSENCE of isotherm or kinetics fitting - no Langmuir, no Freundlich, no adsorption kinetics, no structural modelling - which their own single-metal data would have supported. That is the gap a rigorous team exploits, and it is the strongest argument for Concept A's realistic publication route.

priorArt.axis: gallium-binding peptides and real industrial wastewater - the metal side of Concept A
priorArt.citation: Schonberger N, Taylor C, Schrader M, Drobot B, Matys S, Lederer FL, Pollmann K (2021). Gallium-binding peptides as a tool for the sustainable treatment of industrial waste streams. Journal of Hazardous Materials 414:125366.
priorArt.whatItDid: Five Ga-binding peptides (TMHHAAIAHPPH, NYLPHQSSSPSR, SQALSTSRQDLR, HTQHIQSDDHLA, NDLQRHRLTAGP) characterised by isothermal titration microcalorimetry and computational modelling, then immobilised on polystyrene beads as a robust biosorbent. Validated with a REAL industrial wastewater sample. NYLPHQSSSPSR had the highest Ga affinity. Ga/As discrimination addressed explicitly.
priorArt.whyItMatters: The peptide sequences Concept A would need already exist, are published, and are already validated on real industrial wastewater on a solid support. Concept A inherits this rather than discovering it - which is good for feasibility and bad for novelty. Note also the paper's stated reason for leaving phage behind: phage particles lack the stability for industrial processes. That argues for display on a robust host or for secreted peptide on a support, not phage.

priorArt.axis: gallium-binding peptide discovery and engineering
priorArt.citation: Schonberger N, Zeitler C, Braun R, Lederer FL, Matys S, Pollmann K (2019). Directed Evolution and Engineering of Gallium-Binding Phage Clones - A Preliminary Study. Biomimetics 4(2):35.
priorArt.whatItDid: Phage surface display selection of Ga-binding peptides; systematic cysteine scanning showed that constraining peptide flexibility with a disulfide bridge shifts selectivity strongly, either towards Ga over As or the reverse, depending on cysteine position.
priorArt.whyItMatters: Establishes that Ga-binding peptide selectivity is tunable by conformational constraint. Mechanistically suggestive for a photoswitch approach - a photoswitch is also a conformational constraint - but nobody has made that connection experimentally, which is part of why the gap is real.

priorArt.axis: engineered PROTEIN binders for gallium and indium specifically
priorArt.citation: Ghosh P, et al. (2024). Engineered Nanobodies Bind Bismuth, Indium and Gallium for Applications in Theranostics. Angewandte Chemie International Edition.
priorArt.whatItDid: Single-residue mutagenesis creates a triple-cysteine motif binding Bi; two mutations create a quadruple-cysteine mutant specific for Ga and In. Labelling quantitative in minutes; stable for weeks; resists competition from glutathione.
priorArt.whyItMatters: Engineered protein binders for Ga and In already exist and are selective and robust. So 'an engineered protein that binds gallium or indium' is NOT new. Only the light-gating of such a protein is.

priorArt.axis: whole-cell display + metal binding + isotherms + regeneration, done properly
priorArt.citation: Li Q, Wang Y, Zeng C, Wu Z, Chen W, Wang D (2026). Integrated detection and recovery of light/medium rare earth elements using Hans-LanM-based fluorescent probe and whole-cell adsorbent. Journal of Hazardous Materials 515:143117.
priorArt.whatItDid: Hans-LanM inserted into sfGFP gives a probe with picomolar affinity and 2 nM Sm3+ detection limit; the fusion displayed on E. coli gives a whole-cell adsorbent. 81.5% Nd3+ and 72.6% Sm3+ vs 32% Y3+ at 500 uM; equilibrium capacity 150 mg/g Sm3+; equilibrium in 30 min; selective (55-70%) in real soil leachate against a 10^6-fold excess of competing ions; >85% desorption at pH 2.3; >60% retained after 5 cycles; quasi-second-order kinetics; fluorescence linear with adsorbed amount for real-time monitoring.
priorArt.whyItMatters: This is the standard Concept A would be measured against, and it is high. It also shows the quality bar for the rigour route: isotherms, kinetics, cycling, selectivity in a real matrix, and a built-in optical readout. Note the elution is pH 2.3 acid - which is exactly the step Concept A proposes to replace with light. So the problem Concept A attacks is real and current.

priorArt.axis: de novo photoswitch-protein binder pairs - the method that would actually be needed
priorArt.citation: Miyazaki T, et al. (2026). De novo chemo-optogenetics through the rational design of photoresponsive molecules and selection of their artificial protein binding pairs. Nature Chemistry.
priorArt.whatItDid: Designs a synthetic photoswitch with defined properties first, then uses mRNA display to select artificial protein binders recognising a specific photoisomer-dependent conformation. Yields programmable photoswitch-protein binder pairs with sustained, reversible or repeatable regulatory modes.
priorArt.whyItMatters: This is the state of the art in making a protein's binding light-dependent on purpose. It needs mRNA display and synthetic chemistry. It is a direct measure of how far outside a high-school season the genuinely novel version of Concept A sits.

priorArt.axis: light-switchable protein binders (the LOV route)
priorArt.citation: Opto-nanobodies (OptoNBs): Optogenetic control of protein binding using light-switchable nanobodies (2020), Nature Communications; preprint bioRxiv 739201.
priorArt.whatItDid: LOV-domain insertion into nanobodies makes binding to untagged protein targets reversibly light-dependent.
priorArt.whyItMatters: Proves the design logic (photoswitch domain fused into a binder changes affinity with light) works for protein targets. Nobody has transferred it to a metal-binding protein. That transfer is the novel claim available to Concept A.
priorArt.unverified: Exact author list, year and DOI not confirmed; verify before citing.

priorArt.axis: microbial recovery of Ga and In - the well-trodden baseline

citations.citation: Saikia S, Costa RB, Sinharoy A, Cunha MP, Zaiat M, Lens PNL (2022). Selective removal and recovery of gallium and germanium from synthetic zinc refinery residues using biosorption and bioprecipitation. Journal of Environmental Management 317:115396.
citations.note: Biosorption of Ga onto biogenic elemental Te gave 69 +/- 0.4% removal, 74 mg Ga/g. Notably NO method recovered germanium - relevant to the choice of target metal.

citations.citation: Pourhossein F, Mousavi SM (2018). Enhancement of copper, nickel, and gallium recovery from LED waste by adaptation of Acidithiobacillus ferrooxidans. Waste Management 79:98-108.
citations.note: 60% Ga bioleaching from LED powder. Bioleaching, not binding - and Acidithiobacillus is outside the team's RG1 organism list.

citations.citation: Constantin A, Pourhossein F, Ray D, Farnaud S (2024). Investigating the acidophilic microbial community's adaptation for enhancement indium bioleaching from high pulp density shredded discarded LCD panels. Journal of Environmental Management 365:121521.
citations.note: Up to 100% indium bioleaching from powdered LCD panels.

citations.citation: Pennesi C, Amato A, Occhialini S, Critchley AT, Totti C, Giorgini E, Conti C, Beolchini F (2019). Adsorption of indium by waste biomass of brown alga Ascophyllum nodosum. Scientific Reports 9:16763.
citations.note: 48-63 mg/g indium, optimum pH 3, with explicit Fe/In competition analysis. A good model for how an isotherm-and-competition paper is structured.

citations.citation: Zheng KC, et al. (2023). Recovery technologies for indium, gallium, and germanium from end-of-life products (electronic waste) - A review. Journal of Environmental Management.
citations.note: Review; 142 citations. Establishes that indirect bioleaching reaches ~70% Ga extraction yield and that hydrometallurgy dominates. Cite this to show the team knows the baseline.

citations.citation: Son S, et al. (2025). Solar-assisted Bioelectrochemical Removal and Solid-phase Capture of Critical Group-13 Metals: Indium and Gallium. Journal of Electrochemical Science and Technology.
citations.note: Uses a REAL Ga-bearing semiconductor effluent (1016 +/- 4 mg/L) with a PV-biased bioanode reactor; 88% Ga removal at ~1.25 V. Light is used as an ENERGY source here, not as a control signal - a distinction Concept A should draw explicitly, because a reviewer will otherwise conflate them.

whatIsNew.theOneGenuineGap: No published work makes a PROTEIN's affinity for a technologically critical metal ion (Ga, In, Ge) switchable by light, so that the metal itself is captured and released on an optical signal. Four independent searches across PubMed, Consensus and the open web failed to find it. Photoswitchable metal binding exists in synthetic materials (spiropyran sponges, azobenzene cages, isatin hydrazones); light-switchable protein binding exists for PROTEIN targets (Azo-tag, OptoNBs, de novo chemo-optogenetics); engineered protein binders for Ga and In exist but are not light-gated. The intersection is empty.
whatIsNew.scopeOfTheClaim: This is a 'nobody has published this' claim, but about a narrow intersection, not a field. Phrase it as the intersection, never as 'light-controlled metal recovery', which is published.
whatIsNew.secondaryGap: No whole-cell Ga biosorbent has been characterised with full isotherm, kinetic, selectivity-against-Al-and-Fe and multi-cycle regeneration data at semiconductor-effluent-relevant concentrations (1-35 mg/L). The Schonberger work is peptide-on-beads; the Li 2026 work is whole-cell but for rare earths. This is a 'nobody has published this at this rigour' claim, and it is the one the team can actually deliver.

whatIsNotNew: Light instead of chemical elution in affinity chromatography - published three separate ways (Mayrhofer 2024 Nat Commun; Prodromou 2023 Adv Funct Mater; Agrawal 2026 Curr Protoc). Do not claim this framing.

Light-modulated reversible capture and release of metal ions - published in synthetic materials (Mutluturk 2025 spiropyran-PDMS; Ghosh 2026 metal-organic capsules including photoswitchable Li extraction).

Optogenetic control of a microbial metal-recovery process - published (McGill iGEM 2026) and the light-harvesting mechanism itself is published from 2016 with the team's own CcaSR system (Nakajima 2016).
Microbial surface display for selective metal binding - thoroughly established; McGill 2026, Li 2026, and a large biosorption literature.
Gallium-binding peptides, including validation on real industrial wastewater - published (Schonberger 2019, 2021).
Engineered protein binders selective for Ga and In - published (Ghosh 2024 Angew Chem).
Biosorption and bioleaching of Ga and In from wastes - very thoroughly done; a review with 142 citations already exists (Zheng 2023).
Using light as an energy input to a metal-recovery reactor - published (Son 2025, PV-biased bioelectrochemical system on real semiconductor effluent).

criticalFeasibilityWarning.theCategoryError: CcaSR is a TRANSCRIPTIONAL switch. It controls gene expression, not protein conformation. It cannot gate the binding affinity of an already-folded, already-displayed protein. Using CcaSR, light can only change how much binder is MADE - it cannot release metal already bound. A report that says 'we will use our CcaSR system to control binding and release' will be read by any reviewer or judge as a misunderstanding of the team's own tool. This must be fixed in the write-up regardless of which concept is chosen.
criticalFeasibilityWarning.whatWouldActuallyBeRequired: A genuine light-gated metal binder needs either (a) unnatural amino acid incorporation of a photoswitchable side chain, as in the Azo-tag - amber suppression plus Pap synthesis, not realistic for a high-school season; or (b) inserting a LOV or other photoswitch domain into a metal-binding protein and screening variants for a light-dependent affinity shift, as OptoNBs did for protein targets - conceptually accessible, but needs many rounds of screening and a quantitative binding assay to detect what will probably be a small affinity change; or (c) de novo photoswitch-binder selection by mRNA display (Miyazaki 2026) - far out of scope.
criticalFeasibilityWarning.honestAssessment: Route (b) is the only one a well-supported high-school team could attempt, and one season is realistically enough to build the constructs and get a preliminary, probably negative or ambiguous, result. The team should plan for the fallback being the publishable output, not the stretch goal.

feasibility.verdict: The genuinely novel part is NOT feasible in one high-school season. The rigour fallback IS feasible and is publishable.
achievableInOneSeason: Express and display or secrete a published Ga-binding peptide (NYLPHQSSSPSR is the best-characterised) in E. coli or B. subtilis WB800. WB800 is extracellular-protease-deficient, which is a genuine advantage for a secreted binder and a point the team can make.
Full equilibrium isotherms (Langmuir and Freundlich) and kinetics (pseudo-first and pseudo-second order) for Ga3+ at 1-35 mg/L, the documented fab-effluent range.
Selectivity against Al3+ and Fe3+ - the metals that actually compete with Ga and the ones that defeat most Ga-selective reagents. This is the measurement that would most distinguish the work.
Multi-cycle regeneration with acid elution, as the honest baseline against which any light effect would later be compared.

A CcaSR-controlled expression circuit for the binder, correctly described as light-controlled PRODUCTION, not light-controlled release. This is still a real and interesting dose-control result, and it plays to the team's Best Measurement strength.
Build the LOV-insertion library and report it as preliminary, with honest negative results if that is what comes out.
notAchievable: A working light-gated metal-binding protein with demonstrated release. Treat as a multi-year goal.

Real semiconductor process effluent in a school lab. The team should use a synthetic matrix that mimics the published composition (Ga3+ in acidic sulfate or chloride with Al and Fe competitors) and say so plainly. This also respects the no-environmental-samples constraint.
feasibility.constraintCompliance: Fully compliant. E. coli and B. subtilis WB800 are RG1; no human samples; no environmental isolation needed because the peptide sequences are published; nothing leaves the lab.

instrumentNeeded.goldStandard: ICP-MS or ICP-OES for Ga quantification. This is what every paper cited here uses, and a reviewer will expect it for any capacity number that carries a decimal point. A single university collaboration for ICP-OES runs would materially raise the ceiling of this project.

colorimetricAndFluorimetricAlternatives.verdict: A validated low-instrument route EXISTS and is adequate for the 1-35 mg/L fab-effluent range, but selectivity is the catch.

options.reportedPerformance: A fibre-optic time-resolved fluorescence sensor using 30 uM lumogallion at pH 5 reported a Ga detection limit of 2e-5 M, which is approximately 1.4 mg/L.
options.assessment: Sensitivity is adequate for 1-35 mg/L but only just. The serious problem is that lumogallion binds Al3+ strongly - it is in fact a standard aluminium reagent - so in any matrix containing Al it is not Ga-selective. Masking or separation would be required.
options.unverified: No dedicated analytical validation study for a lumogallion Ga method was found. Detection limits in the sources use different definitions and matrices and are not directly comparable.

options.reportedPerformance: LOD 7.6 ug/L, LOQ 25 ug/L, linear range 34.9-418.3 ug/L.
options.assessment: Far more sensitive than needed, so samples would be diluted into range - which is good, because dilution also reduces matrix interference. The most promising low-cost option. Needs its own selectivity validation against Al and Fe in the team's matrix.

options.reportedPerformance: 3-sigma detection limit 7.17 nM (0.50 ug/L), from 11 replicates at 20 ug/L, in synthetic U-Ga and Ga-As solutions.
options.assessment: Validated in synthetic solutions including Ga-As, which is the relevant interferent pair for GaAs fab waste. Worth reading closely.

colorimetricAndFluorimetricAlternatives.theRealOpportunity: Validating a colorimetric or fluorimetric Ga method against ICP for a defined synthetic fab-effluent matrix, with a documented Al and Fe interference profile, is itself a publishable measurement contribution - and it is squarely in the team's Best Measurement wheelhouse. It may be a better primary objective than the biology.
colorimetricAndFluorimetricAlternatives.optionToConsider: Li 2026 built the readout into the binder by inserting the metal-binding domain into sfGFP, giving fluorescence linear with adsorbed metal. A Ga-binding-peptide-in-fluorescent-protein sensor is a legitimate, achievable and somewhat novel design that would give the team a self-reporting adsorbent and a measurement story at once.

publicationVenues.realistic: Only with ICP-grade quantification and a complete isotherm, kinetics, selectivity and cycling dataset. This is where Schonberger 2021 and Li 2026 both published, so it is the right target for the rigour route - but it is a high bar for a high-school team working alone.
More accessible than J Hazard Mater for a careful, well-controlled, modest-scope biosorption study. Hydrometallurgy in particular values complete isotherm and selectivity data over novelty.

Good fit for the colorimetric-Ga-method validation, which may be the team's strongest single deliverable. Measurement rigour is the currency here, and the team has already been recognised for exactly that.

publicationVenues.venue: ACS Synthetic Biology, or Journal of Biological Engineering
publicationVenues.realistic: For the CcaSR-controlled binder-expression circuit, honestly framed as dose control rather than release control. Modest but real.

Certain, and should be done regardless. A well-characterised B. subtilis WB800 secreted Ga-binding-peptide part with real binding data would be genuinely useful to other teams and is the lowest-risk publication-shaped output.

The right home for the LOV-insertion attempt if it gives preliminary or negative results. A clean negative result on light-gating a metal binder is genuinely useful to the field and costs nothing to post.

strongestNoveltyClaim.claim: Light-switchable protein-ligand pairs have been demonstrated for protein targets, and photoswitchable metal-ion capture for synthetic polymers and coordination cages, but no engineered protein has been reported whose affinity for a technologically critical p-block metal ion is gated by light; we report the first attempt to transfer the photoswitch-insertion strategy from protein binders to a gallium-binding peptide, together with a complete equilibrium, kinetic and Al/Fe-selectivity characterisation of the unswitched binder at semiconductor-effluent-relevant concentrations.
strongestNoveltyClaim.whyThisSurvivesPeerReview: It concedes everything that is published, in the same sentence. It makes the novelty claim about a specific intersection rather than a field. And it does not depend on the light-gating succeeding - the characterisation stands on its own, so the paper is publishable either way.
whatNotToClaim: Do NOT write 'the first light-controlled metal capture and release'. Mutluturk 2025 and Ghosh 2026 refute it.
Do NOT write 'regenerating a recovery column with light instead of acid elution, for the first time'. Mayrhofer 2024 refutes it.
Do NOT write 'the first optogenetic control of microbial metal recovery'. McGill iGEM 2026 refutes it, and Nakajima 2016 refutes the mechanism.
Do NOT write 'the first engineered protein binder for gallium'. Ghosh 2024 and Schonberger 2019 refute it.

A.verdictReasoning: The light-gated-metal-binding-protein intersection is genuinely unoccupied and that is a real finding. But the concept as a whole is surrounded on every side: the light-elution framing, the photoswitchable metal capture, the optogenetic metal-recovery project, the Ga-binding peptides and the Ga/In protein binders are all published. The remaining gap is exactly what the coordinator suspected: light controls release of the metal rather than harvesting of the cells. That gap is narrow, real, and not reachable in one season. Describe it as narrow, not as open ground.
unverified: DOIs not captured for: Prodromou 2023 Adv Funct Mater; Agrawal 2026 Curr Protoc; Mutluturk 2025 ACS Appl Polym Mater; Ghosh 2026 Acc Chem Res; Ghosh 2024 Angew Chem; Miyazaki 2026 Nat Chem; Son 2025 J Electrochem Sci Technol. Exact citation for the OptoNB paper (authors, year, DOI) not confirmed.

Whether the Helmholtz Freiberg group has since moved from peptide-on-beads to bacterial surface display of Ga-binding peptides. Searches found only phage display and bead immobilisation. If they have, it would narrow Concept A's fallback significantly, so check Franziska Lederer's publication list directly before committing.
Whether any patent (as opposed to paper) claims light-gated metal binding by a protein. Patent databases were not systematically searched. This matters for any entrepreneurship framing.
