pfasUsesInFabs.authoritativeSource: The Semiconductor PFAS Consortium's ten technical white papers, indexed at https://www.semiconductors.org/pfas/
pfasUsesInFabs.sevenApplicationAreas: photolithography; wet chemical processing; plasma-enabled etch and deposition; heat transfer fluids; lubricants; assembly/test/packaging; and articles. https://www.semiconductors.org/wp-content/uploads/2023/05/FINAL-PFAS-Consortium-Background-Paper.pdf
pfasUsesInFabs.photolithographyVerifiedInDetail: Photoacid generators are components of chemically amplified resists, chemically amplified polybenzoxazoles/polyimides and bottom anti-reflective coatings. The predominant PAGs are sulfonium or iodonium salts paired with PFAS super-acid anions, and the paper states 'all successfully demonstrated PAGs for high performance resists are fluorinated.' Both TARCs and BARCs are fluorinated for low refractive index and low surface energy. PFAS surfactants appear in BARCs, TARCs, colour-filter resists and rinses, including first-generation EUV rinses. THE RELEASE PATHWAY IS EXPLICIT: aqueous developer and rinse streams 'typically drain to wastewater' while solvent developer is collected separately - that is the mechanistic link from lithography to the fab drain. https://www.semiconductors.org/wp-content/uploads/2023/09/PFAS-Release-Mapping-from-Semiconductor-Photolithography-Processes-Rev.0.pdf
pfasUsesInFabs.wetEtchantsPrecision: Buffered HF used in buffered oxide etch 'is supplied both with and without a surfactant because not all applications using BHF require it': PFAS surfactant may be unnecessary at a 2:1 aspect ratio but essential at 10:1 (50 nm wide by 500 nm deep). So PFAS in BOE is application-specific, not universal. https://www.semiconductors.org/wp-content/uploads/2023/08/FINAL-PFAS-Containing-Wet-Chemistries-Used-in-Semiconductor-Manufacturing.pdf
pfasUsesInFabs.plasmaEtchCVD: HFCs (CHF3, CH2F2) and PFCs (CF4, C4F8, c-C4F8) fall inside the Consortium's PFAS definition.
pfasUsesInFabs.peerReviewedCounterweight: Ober, Kafer & Deng (2022). Review of essential use of fluorochemicals in lithographic patterning and semiconductor processing. J. Micro/Nanopattern. Mater. Metrol. 21(1):010901. https://doi.org/10.1117/1.JMM.21.1.010901
pfasUsesInFabs.WARNING_thousandsOfApplications: 'Thousands of applications' is an industry characterisation with NO published basis - do not use it as a figure. SIA's press release says PFAS are used in 'thousands of essential applications' but gives no count, methodology or breakdown. The only defensible count is the Consortium's own survey: of 28 distinct wet chemical formulations surveyed, 16 (57%) contained no PFAS and 9 (32%) are produced both with and without a PFAS component - and the paper itself warns responses were limited to participating members.

pfasConsortium.claim: Hosted by the Semiconductor Industry Association - stated verbatim in the Background Paper: 'organized under the auspices of the Semiconductor Industry Association (SIA).' It explicitly disclaims advocacy: it 'DOES NOT lobby government officials or undertake policymaking'; SIA, ESIA and SEMI advocate using its outputs. Membership: 38 named members on the July 2024 list - AND TSMC IS ONE, which is directly relevant to a Taiwanese team. Others include Applied Materials, ASML, BASF, Chemours, DuPont, Entegris, GlobalFoundries, IBM, Intel, JSR, Lam Research, Micron, NXP, Bosch, Samsung Austin, ST, TI, Tokyo Electron, TOK, ZEISS.
pfasConsortium.caveats: Formation date 'January 2022' is secondary only (SEMI presentation decks; semi.org returned 403). SIA's own documents give no formation date; the Aug 2023 release says Phase 1 took 18 months, which back-calculates consistently - write 'formed in early 2022'. Member counts disagree across SIA's own documents: 38 (May 2023), 42 (Aug 2023 release), 38 (July 2024). Cite the July 2024 list as current.
pfasConsortium.mostReportRelevantPublication: '2023 Survey Results - PFAS in Semiconductor Fabrication Facility Wastewater': 26 facilities, 7 member companies, across the US, Europe and Asia; targeted PFAS discharges 0.002-13 g/day per facility, averaging about 4 g/day (about 3.2 lb/yr). TWO CAVEATS MUST TRAVEL WITH THAT NUMBER: these are MASS LOADS, not concentrations, so they cannot be compared against any ng/L standard; and SIA itself states current target analytical methods cannot characterise some PFAS species present, making it a LOWER BOUND. https://www.semiconductors.org/consortium-publishes-survey-results-of-pfas-discharges-to-wastewater/

fluorideConcentrations.recommendedPrimaryFigure: Semiconductors and displays, 300-1,200 mg/L. Sinharoy & Chung (2024). Fluoride removal from wastewater and potential for resource recovery. Environmental Engineering Research 29(6):240179, open access. Also gives electrical/electronics 300-4,500 mg/L and steelmaking 6,500-130,000 mg/L for contrast, and notes many regulators cap discharge at under 15 mg/L - which matches Taiwan exactly. https://www.eeer.org/journal/view.php?number=1574
fluorideConcentrations.measuredSinglePlantFigure: A semiconductor wastewater treated by electrocoagulation-flotation went from 806 mg/L down to 5-6 mg/L. The same review reports that 'almost 30% of waste produced in the semiconductor industry is of fluorine origin.' Materials 15(10):3461 (2022). https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9147173/
fluorideConcentrations.WARNING_dropThisFigure: Drop the commonly-repeated '1,000-3,500 mg/L'. It traces to Huang & Liu, Water Research 33(16):3403-3412 (1999), where it is itself a citation to Chou et al. 1994 describing 'typical wastewater of local semiconductor industry' - i.e. Taiwan in the early 1990s. Chou et al. 1994 could not be retrieved at all; the 1999 full text is paywalled; and another paper citing the same source gives the range as 500-2,000 mg/L, which is inconsistent. Use 300-1,200 mg/L and the measured 806 mg/L instead, noting that segregated high-concentration HF streams run higher than combined effluent.
fluorideConcentrations.noBOESpecificFigure: No HF- or BOE-specific mg/L figure exists in the peer-reviewed literature that could be found - only aggregated 'fluoride wastewater'. Taiwanese thesis literature describes stream segregation into high-concentration (several thousand mg/L, pH 2-5) and low-concentration (mostly under 500 mg/L) fluoride streams, which is fine as supporting colour but not as a headline. The report should not assert a BOE-specific number.
fluorideConcentrations.treatmentAndRecovery: Conventional route is calcium precipitation to CaF2 (lime or CaCl2), usually needing excess calcium, with sludge normally landfilled; fine CaF2 settles poorly, hence coagulants or flotation. Only fluidized-bed crystallization yields a fluoride-rich recoverable product among the technologies compared. A two-stage FBR achieved about 94% fluoride removal, crystallization efficiency over 95% sustained 41 days (peak 98.6%), recovered CaF2 at 91.1% purity, crystals growing 402.7 um to 1,003 um, meeting a 15 mg/L standard (Int. J. Mol. Sci. 25(9):4646, 2024) - but simulated wastewater, lab scale, Korean authors, no Taiwan content, and two unreconciled influent values (300 vs 460 mg/L). The claim of 'three full-scale FBC plants in Hsinchu Science Park' rests on a roughly 23-year-old ResearchGate snippet and is UNVERIFIED - do not use.

caf2SludgeRecoveryInTaiwan.claim: Taiwan dries and granulates CaF2 sludge into artificial fluorite for steelmaking flux. Processor LiYing Environmental Technology, founded 2013, more than 50% of Taiwan's four artificial-fluorite producers, 2024 revenue over NT$200m, processes about 1,500 t/month of CaF2 sludge, about 40% of it from TSMC, yielding about 750 t/month of artificial fluorite at up to 80% purity, at about one-third the cost of natural fluorite (which Taiwan imports almost entirely from China). It operates inside TSMC's Taichung zero-waste centre (commercial operation Nov 2024) and UMC's Nanke circular-economy centre (about 5,000 t/yr). Buyers: China Steel, Formosa Plastics' Vietnam mill, Yieh United Steel.
caf2SludgeRecoveryInTaiwan.caveat: Single business-press source - specific and internally consistent, but secondary.
caf2SludgeRecoveryInTaiwan.whyThisMattersToTheTeam: This is a strong, concrete, Taiwanese circular-economy precedent: a semiconductor waste stream already being valorised at industrial scale, inside TSMC's own facility. It is useful framing for any recovery-themed project and shows the industry is receptive to the idea.

a_fluorideEffluentStandard.claim: Fluoride effluent standard = 15 mg/L, with NO stricter sector-specific limit. Governing regulation: Effluent Standards, last amended 18 December 2024. Verified verbatim from the Executive Yuan Gazette tables (vol. 031 no. 237): fluoride = 15 in Table 1 (wafer and semiconductor manufacturing), Table 2 (optoelectronic materials and devices), Table 9 (science-park dedicated sewer systems), and every other table. So the sector-specific tables EXIST - semiconductors got their own in 2011 precisely because of fluorine-bearing wastewater - but they do not tighten the fluoride number relative to general industry. Other semiconductor-table values: pH 6.0-9.0, nitrate-N 50 mg/L, temperature 38 C or below May-Sep and 35 C or below Oct-Apr. For contrast, Taiwan's DRINKING-WATER fluoride standard is 0.8 mg/L.

b_pfasDrinkingWater.claim: Binding. Drinking Water Quality Standards Art. 3-1, promulgated 25 November 2024: PFOA + PFOS combined 50 ng/L; PFOS + PFHxS combined 70 ng/L; effective 1 July 2027, with interim testing from 1 Jan 2025 and 7-day exceedance notification. A non-binding guideline of 100 ng/L for the sum of 20 PFAS also exists.

c_pfasSurfaceWater.claim: Binding, and new. Surface Water Body Classification and Water Quality Standards amended 25 March 2026, adding a combined PFOA + PFOS criterion of 50 ng/L or below for Class A and Class B water bodies.

d_pfasWastewaterMonitoring_THE_BEST_FACT.claim: Taiwan DOES mandate PFAS wastewater monitoring for fabs, via a different regulation, and this is badly under-reported. The Regulations Governing Water Pollution Control Measures and Testing and Reporting Management, amended 20 January 2025, added Art. 84-3 and Table 6, 'emerging concern items'. Values apply to BOTH raw wastewater and effluent, tested once per year, effective 1 January 2027: PFOS 120 ng/L; PFOA 1,700 ng/L; PFHxS 2,100 ng/L. Covered entities include science-park and industrial-park dedicated sewer systems and - strikingly specific - wafer/semiconductor manufacturing and optoelectronic materials and devices manufacturing that discharge to surface water AND USE PHOTORESIST IN THE PROCESS. Enforcement: two consecutive exceedances trigger a mandatory self-reduction management plan within three months, maximum two years; three consecutive non-exceedances earn a testing exemption.
d_pfasWastewaterMonitoring_THE_BEST_FACT.IMPORTANT_PRECISION: These are MONITORING VALUES triggering a reduction-plan duty, NOT effluent limits carrying a fine. Do not call them 'effluent standards'. PFAS is in fact NOT in the effluent standards: environmental groups asked for PFAS and total organic fluorine limits in the 2024 amendment and MOENV declined, saying PFAS is not yet regulated in effluent standards internationally. The 2024 amendment instead tightened ammonia-N, phosphorus, residual chlorine and copper, affecting over 3,700 businesses, mainly semiconductors, optoelectronics and science parks.

e_monitoringProgramme.claim: MOENV Chemicals Administration, page dated 8 Jan 2026: 4,714 environmental samples analysed in 2024 for background PFAS (river sediments and fish, groundwater, seawater, effluent, drinking water, soil, textiles); 269 PFAS pre-announced as 'chemicals of concern' on 5 August 2025; drinking-water monitoring covering 130 large plants (about 91% of national supply), all compliant; 13 PFAS banned in cosmetics from 1 Jan 2025.

taiwaneseFluorideIncident.verified: Executive Yuan appeal decision 院臺訴字第1090171516號, 30 April 2020: fluoride measured at 18.2 mg/L against the 15 mg/L limit, sampled 17 May 2019 by the EPA's Northern Regional Environmental Inspection Brigade during a public-complaint investigation. Penalty NT$390,000 plus 2 hours mandatory environmental education; appeal dismissed. Legally significant: fluoride is designated a substance hazardous to health by EPA announcement of 25 December 2018, which adds 3 penalty points.
taiwaneseFluorideIncident.IMPORTANT_CAVEAT: The violator is the Guanyin Industrial Zone Service Centre in Taoyuan - an industrial-zone SEWER OPERATOR, not a fab. A real, fully documented Taiwanese fluoride-exceedance enforcement case against a facility receiving industrial wastewater, but NOT a semiconductor plant. Say so.
taiwaneseFluorideIncident.noFabCase: No fluoride-exceedance penalty against a named Taiwanese semiconductor or optoelectronics plant could be found, despite targeted Chinese-language searches of news, EPB penalty announcements and the Thaubing database.
taiwaneseFluorideIncident.CONFLATION_TO_AVOID: The famous ASE Kaohsiung / Houjin River case of October 2013 was an ACIDITY (pH 3.02) and HEAVY-METALS violation, NOT fluoride. (Supreme Administrative Court 106年判字第289號, 8 June 2017.) Separately, Taiwan Semiconductor's Yilan plant was penalised for suspended solids (NT$1.428m, 2021) and for permit/recordkeeping irregularities concerning its fluorine-based wastewater route - a paperwork violation, not a concentration exceedance.

fabLinkedContaminationCase_USE_THIS_INST.claim: For a fab-linked contamination case, the peer-reviewed PFAS river evidence is squarely about Taiwanese semiconductors. Lin, Panchangam & Lo (2009). The impact of semiconductor, electronics and optoelectronic industries on downstream perfluorinated chemical contamination in Taiwanese rivers. Environmental Pollution 157(4):1365-1372: ten PFCs measured in plant wastewater and in the Keya, Touchien and Xiaoli rivers - the HSINCHU SCIENCE PARK CATCHMENT - with PFOS up to 5.4 ug/L (5,400 ng/L) in river water and up to 0.13 mg/L in semiconductor wastewater; the upstream plants identified as the primary cause.
fabLinkedContaminationCase_USE_THIS_INST.companionPaper: Lin, Panchangam & Ciou (2010), Chemosphere 80(10):1167-1174 - photolithographic wastewater contained 12.5 mg/L PFOS; PFC levels about 10,000 ng/L in industrial WWTP effluent and receiving rivers; Nanmen Creek sediment PFOS up to about 90,000 ng/kg; PFOS risk quotient 1.21. This is the number that links lithography chemistry directly to the drain. https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/20643472/
fabLinkedContaminationCase_USE_THIS_INST.MUST_FLAG: Both papers are 2009/2010, BEFORE the PFOS phase-out progressed. The report must NOT present these as current concentrations - flag the vintage explicitly.

euAndUsRestrictions.echaUniversalPfasRestriction: Five submitters: Germany, Netherlands, Denmark, Sweden, Norway; REACH Annex XV report submitted January 2023; updated Background Document incorporates over 5,600 consultation responses. Semiconductors: Annex 2 entry '5.w - Semiconductor manufacturing' (renumbered 5.ee), status 'Potential derogation confirmed', duration 13.5 years after entry into force, covering photolithography, etching, deposition, engineered fluids, equipment and advanced packaging. Sector assessment: restriction option 2 cuts emissions 79%, substitution potential Low, verdict 'Likely proportionate'. Reconciling 12 vs 13.5 years: the 2023 report proposed 12 years; the 2025 document restates it as 13.5 years after entry into force - the same thing inclusive of the 18-month transition. RAC adopted its final opinion 2 March 2026; SEAC agreed its draft 10 March 2026; the 60-day consultation closed 25 May 2026 with 3,511 comments from over 3,200 organisations, and ELECTRONICS AND SEMICONDUCTORS DREW THE LARGEST SECTOR SHARE AT 12.7%.
euAndUsRestrictions.echaAccessCaveat: echa.europa.eu returned HTTP 403 on every path, so no ECHA page is first-hand verified. The substance above is verified from a primary document by one of the five dossier submitters, the Swedish Chemicals Agency (KEMI), updated 23 October 2025. https://www.kemi.se/download/18.43415f2e19a0f60356220f8/1761224887540/What%20you%20need%20to%20know%20about%20the%20updated%20PFAS%20restriction%20dossier-Updated-2025-10-23-2.pdf
euAndUsRestrictions.TIME_CRITICAL: SEAC adopted its FINAL opinion on 19 NOVEMBER 2026 - the day before this verification. It rejected a blanket ban and backed a phased approach: ban in principle 18 months after adoption for consumer uses and sectors with alternatives, plus temporary exemptions of 5 to 12 years for critical industries with no viable alternative, SEMICONDUCTORS EXPLICITLY NAMED. SINGLE SOURCE, ONE DAY OLD, and it reframes the duration as '5 to 12 years' versus KEMI's '6.5 or 13.5 years after entry into force'. Verify on ECHA's own site before publication. Both opinions now go to the Commission; no adoption date is set. https://agenceurope.eu/en/bulletin/article/13985/5/echa-endorses-final-opinion-favouring-targeted-pfas-restrictions
euAndUsRestrictions.usEpaMcls: Fully verified from EPA. 2024 final rule (announced 10 April 2024; Federal Register 26 April 2024): PFOA 4.0 ppt, PFOS 4.0 ppt (MCLG zero for both); PFHxS, PFNA, HFPO-DA (GenX) 10 ppt each; Hazard Index = 1 for the four-way mixture. Monitoring and public reporting by 2027; solutions by 2029. On 14 May 2025 EPA announced it would RETAIN the 4 ppt PFOA/PFOS MCLs. On 18 May 2026 two PROPOSED rules: a compliance extension moving the PFOA/PFOS deadline from 26 April 2029 to 26 April 2031, and a RESCISSION of the PFHxS, PFNA, HFPO-DA and Hazard Index regulations. NEITHER IS FINALISED and litigation over the 2024 rule is active in the D.C. Circuit. State the 4 ppt PFOA/PFOS MCLs as current law and everything else as proposed. https://www.epa.gov/sdwa/and-polyfluoroalkyl-substances-pfas
euAndUsRestrictions.tscaReporting: TSCA section 8(a)(7), 40 CFR Part 705, finalised 11 October 2023 - the rule that actually reaches fabs and their suppliers. Retroactive to 1 January 2011, requiring anyone who manufactured or IMPORTED PFAS or PFAS-containing ARTICLES since then to report chemical identity, uses, volumes, byproducts, health/environmental data, worker exposure and disposal. No de minimis and no small-business exemption in the original rule. THE OPERATIVE DEADLINE IS GENUINELY UNCLEAR after a chain of extensions (Nov 2024, then July 2025, then 13 Oct 2026 for most manufacturers / 13 April 2027 for small businesses reporting only on imported articles, then an April 2026 rule adding 60 days after a forthcoming revision takes effect). Verify before publishing a date. A November 2025 proposal would EXEMPT imported articles - directly relevant to fluoropolymer tubing, valves, gaskets and FOUPs; still a proposal. https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2023-10-11/pdf/2023-22094.pdf

taiwanPositionInAiHardware.theClaimStatedAsItCanHonestlyBeMade: Taiwan sits at the single narrowest point in the AI hardware supply chain: TSMC alone took 72.5% of global foundry revenue in Q2 2026, Taiwan and South Korea between them hold ALL of the world's sub-10nm logic capacity, and Taiwanese firms assemble roughly 90% of the world's AI servers - so an AI accelerator is, at several separate stages, almost certain to pass through Taiwan.

foundryRevenueShare.claim: Q2 2026: global top-10 foundry revenue US$53.49bn (+11.5% QoQ, a record); TSMC about US$40.2bn, +12.1% QoQ, 72.5% share. Samsung 5.9% (US$3.26bn), SMIC 5.4%, UMC 3.9%, GlobalFoundries 3.2%. Trend line: 70.2% (Q2 2025, then a record), about 71% (Q3 2025), 72% (Q1 2026), 72.5% (Q2 2026). TrendForce projected 2026 global foundry revenue at about US$218.8bn, +24.8% YoY, with TSMC growing fastest at about 32%.
foundryRevenueShare.caveat: TrendForce's own arithmetic does not quite close - $40.2bn divided by $53.49bn is about 75%, not 72.5% - so the shares likely use a different denominator than the top-10 total. Quote the share as published and do not recompute it.

leadingEdgeCapacity.WARNING: The commonly-repeated 'TSMC has about 90% of leading-edge (5nm/3nm) capacity' DOES NOT CHECK OUT. It does not appear in TrendForce's or Counterpoint's published figures. Drop it.
whatIsVerifiable: 100% of the world's sub-10nm capacity was in Taiwan (92%) and South Korea (8%) - SIA/BCG, verified verbatim from the primary PDF. BUT this is the 2021 report using about 2019 data - SEVEN YEARS OLD. Date it explicitly. https://www.semiconductors.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/03/SIA-BCG_Global-Value-Chain_2-pager.pdf

The 2024 SIA/BCG report does NOT restate a Taiwan sub-10nm percentage (full PDF extracted and searched; no '69%' and no '92%' appear). It says only that South Korea- and Taiwan-headquartered companies lead the world in advanced node fabrication, and projects the US reaching 28% of sub-10nm capacity by 2032 from 0% in 2022. So the widely-cited 'Taiwan 69% of sub-10nm in 2022' is NOT in the 2024 report and could not be sourced - treat as unsourceable.

TSMC's own revenue mix is the cleanest leading-edge evidence: 7nm and below = 74% of wafer revenue in Q4 2025, with 3nm at 24% and 5nm at 36%; for full-year 2025, 3nm rose from 18% (2024) to 24%, 5nm steady at 36%.
Counterpoint: TSMC likely to hold 87% of smartphone SoC shipments at 5nm and below in 2025 - note this is a SHIPMENT share in ONE application, not a capacity share.
Taiwan's share of ALL foundry capacity about 44% (2024), and of advanced (16/14nm and below) capacity 68% (2023), 66% (2024), 60% forecast by 2027, per TrendForce.
leadingEdgeCapacity.recommendation: Build the leading-edge claim on TSMC's 7nm-and-below = 74% of wafer revenue plus the SIA/BCG 92%-of-sub-10nm figure with its 2021 date shown - and drop any 'TSMC has 90% of leading-edge capacity' line.

advancedPackaging.bestSingleFigure: Taiwan's share of global data-centre AI chip packaging, 77% in 2024, projected to decline moderately to 70% by 2030 (DIGITIMES, sample report dated November 2025). https://www.digitimes.com/reports/ai/2025_ai_chip_packaging/assets/Global%20Data%20Center%20AI%20Chip%20Packaging%20Market%20Forecast%202024-2030(sample).pdf
advancedPackaging.cowos: TSMC CoWoS monthly capacity about 70,000 wafers (2025) rising to 130,000-140,000 by end-2026 (TrendForce). NVIDIA has reportedly reserved about 800,000-850,000 wafers of TSMC's 2026 CoWoS capacity, over 50% of the total. TrendForce estimates the CoWoS supply-demand gap will stay at about 20% in 2026. FORECASTS DIVERGE WIDELY: DIGITIMES projects only 88,000 wafers/month by end-2026 (+26% YoY) against TrendForce's 130,000-140,000. Cite a range and name the house.
advancedPackaging.osat: ASE is the world's largest OSAT, over 30% global share, about US$20.78bn 2025 revenue; TrendForce put the top-10 OSATs at US$41.56bn in 2024 with ASE at US$18.54bn (about 45% of the top 10). Taiwan holds 'nearly half' of the global OSAT market. Those three denominators differ - total OSAT market, top-10 revenue, and capacity - so do not blend them.
advancedPackaging.gap: No SEMI figure for Taiwan's share of global advanced packaging CAPACITY in 2025 could be found. Use the DIGITIMES 77% AI-packaging figure and label its scope precisely.

aiServers.claim: Taiwan assembles more than 90% of global AI servers - the original attribution is Taiwan's Ministry of Economic Affairs, reported by DIGITIMES in March 2024, and restated for 2025 in a June 2026 report. Taiwan also makes about 80-83% of ALL servers (not just AI servers), MOEA-sourced - keep the two distinct. Foxconn alone holds about 40% of the global AI server market (TVBS, April and June 2026). Taiwan's Market Intelligence Centre expects AI server shipments of 4.6 million units in 2026, with Taiwan remaining the main production base; the 90% share is expected to decline as manufacturers expand overseas.
aiServers.caveat: No source gives individual AI-server shares for Quanta, Wistron or Inventec, so the four-firm total is UNVERIFIED. State the Taiwan-level 90% and Foxconn's about 40%, and do not sum the four. Wistron overtaking Quanta as Taiwan's second-largest ODM by revenue (2025 revenue over NT$2.19 trillion) is a REVENUE ranking, not a server-share figure, and the source is weak (a LinkedIn post).

abfSubstrate.whatCanBeSaid: Taiwan ranks No. 1 worldwide in ABF substrate market share - but only the headline was retrievable, not the underlying numbers. Unimicron, Ibiden and Shinko together are about three-quarters of the substrate market 'by most estimates' - a three-company figure spanning Taiwan and Japan, not a Taiwan total. DIGITIMES confirms Taiwan's three ABF leaders - Unimicron, Kinsus, Nan Ya PCB - grew at double-digit annual rates in 2025, but gives no shares.
abfSubstrate.doNotUse: Unimicron at 22% appears in a market FAQ with no clear date or methodology - unverified, do not use.
abfSubstrate.recommendation: Either omit a numeric ABF claim or state only 'Taiwan ranks first in ABF substrate share' with the headline citation and an explicit note that the figure is paywalled (TrendForce/Yole).

reclaimedWafers.verdict: Partly realistic, but NOT in the way the premise assumes. Taiwan genuinely is a world centre of wafer reclaim - that part is solid and well documented. But Taiwanese reclaim is a B2B contract business selling to TSMC, Micron and similar, with NO retail channel, and published per-wafer prices essentially do not exist in Taiwan. The cheap, buyable-in-ones-and-twos wafers the premise imagines are a US/EU retail phenomenon, and they are VIRGIN test/dummy wafers, not industrially reclaimed ones. A school can realistically get wafers - most likely by importing from a US/EU research retailer at roughly US$5-40 per small wafer, or by borrowing from a university contact.

taiwaneseReclaimIndustry.company: Phoenix Silicon International / 昇陽半導體 (TPE: 8028)

Described as world No. 2 in Jan 2025 and as having overtaken Japan's RS Technologies to become world No. 1 by Oct 2025. 2025 shipments about 9.486m 12-inch-equivalent wafers, +38.1% on 2024.

'TSMC has about 90% of leading-edge capacity' - not in TrendForce's or Counterpoint's published figures. Use TSMC's 7nm-and-below = 74% of wafer revenue instead.
'Taiwan 69% of sub-10nm capacity (2022)' - not in the 2024 SIA/BCG report (full PDF extracted and searched). Use the 2021 report's 92%, dated.

Fluoride '1,000-3,500 mg/L' in fab wastewater - traces to a 1994 Taiwanese source that could not be obtained, cited second-hand in a paywalled 1999 paper, and contradicted by another citation of the same source (500-2,000 mg/L). Use 300-1,200 mg/L and the measured 806 mg/L.
'Semiconductors take 10% of Taiwan's water' - collides with the WRA split in which 10% is ALL industry. Use absolute volumes instead.
